title: The bottom-field finite free-root unit is an isomorphism
statement: Let l be prime, X any scheme, and n >= 0. Use the bottom finite subextension and finite integral twist coefficients of [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-diagrams] and [sk-def-sp-tate-twist]. The unit of the free/forget adjunction for the pulled-back coefficient spEllPointRingObj l (bottomField l) n, evaluated on the sheaf of l^(n+1)-th roots of unity, is an isomorphism of abelian sheaves. No condition of invertibility of l, no Noetherian hypothesis, no completed coefficient isomorphism and no inverse limit is involved.

source.place: Finite-level tensor formula and base-field coefficient specialization.

proof.text: Use the integral ring equivalence of lem-sfb-base-coefficient-condensed-identification. It sends the principal ideal generated by l^(n+1) to the corresponding principal ideal in the bottom-field integers. Ideal.quotientEquiv, PadicInt.ker_toZModPow and the first isomorphism theorem identify spEllQuotient at the bottom field with ZMod (l^(n+1)), as a unital ring.

The finite quotient is finite and discrete by the finite-level Tate coefficient construction. Apply the finite discrete condensed-ring comparison and its scheme pullback comparison. Compose with the sheafification of the constant ring isomorphism from the preceding step. This identifies the specified pulled-back coefficient with the sheafified constant cyclic ring by an isomorphism preserving the unit.

For any abelian group M killed by N, use its ZMod N module structure. The inverse to m -> 1 tensor m is the integer-balanced lift of (r,m) -> r*m. One composite is one_smul. For the other, write r as an integer residue and move the integer across the tensor sign. Thus the insertion is an isomorphism, including N=0. Apply this sectionwise to an N-torsion abelian sheaf. Strong monoidal sheafification carries the isomorphism of the ring-unit tensor maps to the same map for the sheafified ring; the sheafification counit identifies the sheafification of the original sheaf with itself.

The root sheaf is killed by N=l^(n+1), by its kernel inclusion into units. Apply the preceding tensor calculation. Transport its unit tensor map along the unital coefficient isomorphism from step 2. The actual free/forget adjunction unit is the composite of the inverse left unitor, this unit tensor map, and an identity, so it is invertible. No invertibility of l on X or root generator is used.

proof_origin.place: Finite-level tensor formula and base-field coefficient specialization, implemented by quotient ring equivalences, explicit integer tensor inverses, and strong monoidal sheafification.

mathlib_searches.results: Read DiagonalIntegralRootMap, ProEtaleTateTwistLevels, ConstantZModScalarTensor, both torsion module APIs and BaseCoefficientCondensedIdentification. The tensor comparison has no normalization identifying the free unit. The integral-root-map theorem specifies a map, but not linearity. Blueprint-wide searches returned no duplicate.

lean.statement:
theorem bottomFiniteRootUnit_isIso (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (n : ℕ) :
    IsIso ((Mod.freeForgetAdjunction
      (C := Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj (spEllPointRingObj l ⟨⊥, inferInstance⟩ n) X)).unit.app
        (Scheme.proEtaleRootsOfUnitySheaf X (l ^ (n + 1))))
